To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the value of existing generation assets is not significantly affected by a carbon dioxide emissions trading scheme, (b) the price of allowances will be determined by market forces and (c) the price of carbon dioxide emissions allowances is unlikely to rise above the level that would allow the existing generation fleet to be replaced by new gas-fired generation.

(1) the allocation of carbon dioxide emission allowances to existing generators is not necessary to protect the value of their assets, and (2) the auction of carbon dioxide emission permits is the most efficient method of allocating allowances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how carbon dioxide emission allowance allocation rules affect the asset values of generation assets.
the effects of a carbon dioxide emissions trading scheme on the value of electricity generators, both new and existing.
the impact on the asset values of power generation plants of the distribution of carbon dioxide emission allowances, and in particular the impact of the method of distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

The value of a carbon dioxide emission allowance is the difference between the value of the marginal abatement cost of the last tonne of carbon dioxide abated by a marginal unit, and the value of the carbon dioxide emission allowance.
the auction of carbon dioxide emission allowances is a good idea.
the allocation of allowances is not the most important issue in designing the carbon dioxide emission trading scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while the auctioning of carbon allowances will have an impact on asset values, the impact will be less than the cost of carbon.
the allocation of carbon dioxide emission allowances is a matter of political choice and not a technical necessity.

, in the short run, the allocation method has a significant effect on the distribution of wealth between generators, and that the effect is more pronounced the higher the carbon dioxide emission allowance price is.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not necessary to give away allowances for free to avoid the “carbon leakage” problem.
the allocation of allowances should be done in a way that is consistent with the objective of the policy, and not to protect existing assets from the consequences of the policy.
it is not the price of the allowance but the allocation method that determines the impact on the value of the assets.
